bullets.text: Trump has threatened to bomb Oman, a US ally, if it interferes with an Iran deal, as a 60-day window for peace negotiations expires. He also stated the US would reduce military drills with South Korea after it stayed out of the Iran conflict.
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the deadliest in the country's history, with over 2,325 deaths and the virus spreading to a sixth province.

Russia and Ukraine have traded more deadly strikes, with Moscow reporting nine deaths and Kyiv reporting four. Additionally, Russia's prominent anti-war politician, Lev Schlosberg, was jailed for 11 years for "discrediting" the army.

Angus Taylor has issued an ultimatum to the prime minister, stating that the opposition's support for the National Disability Insurance Scheme is dependent on the government eliminating the 'widows' tax'.
A pygmy blue whale has died after stranding off Groote Eylandt, marking what researchers believe is the first sighting of the species in the Gulf of Carpentaria.
Alarm has been raised over the 'privacy dilemma' of facial recognition technology being used at Coles and Woolworths, with experts warning it is 'normalising surveillance'.
FT analysis indicates that private credit markets are experiencing stress levels not seen since 2017, as troubled loans continue to increase.
Goldman Sachs plans to acquire ETF provider Neos in a deal valued at up to $2.25 billion, expanding its presence in the asset management sector.
Grupo Casas Bahia SA has filed for bankruptcy protection in Sao Paulo, as an out-of-court debt restructuring failed to resolve its financial difficulties amidst high interest rates and tight credit.
